title: Integrability of the centred exponential moment
statement: Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a measure space, let $X\colon\Omega\to\bbr$ be a measurable function, and let $t\in\bbr$. Write $\Lambda(t)$ for the cumulant generating function of $X$ under $\mu$, that is, the logarithm of the moment generating function evaluated at $t$. If the function $x\mapsto e^{t\,X(x)}$ is $\mu$-integrable, then so is the function $x\mapsto e^{t\,X(x)-\Lambda(t)}$.
hypotheses_covered: X is a real-valued function on a measure space with measure μ
t is a fixed real number
replaced: If $e^{tX}$ is $\mu$-integrable, then so is $x \mapsto e^{t X(x) - \Lambda_\mu(t)}$.
